chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in the blind man leading the people in prayer, even if they are the ones who direct him."

key_terms.بِالْقَوْمِ: With the people / leading the congregation

ai.seo_question: Can a blind person lead congregational prayer if others guide him?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of a blind person leading congregational prayer, emphasizing that physical sight is not a prerequisite for spiritual authority in prayer. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing the congregation to guide the imam, thereby ensuring the validity of the prayer even if the imam relies on others for orientation.
